documents.title: League of Nations Treaty Series, No. 2960, volume 129: Exchange of Notes respecting the Boundary between the Mandated Territory of South West Africa and Angola, with the Kakeri Final Act and annexes
documents.publisher: League of Nations Secretariat; volume digitally served by the United Nations Treaty Collection
relevant_content: The English and Portuguese texts identify the Kakeri Final Act as dated 23 September 1928 and include its schedules.
The joint commission says the boundary was demarcated by chords joining 47 main beacons, gives the beacon positions and distances, and locates beacon 47 at Kakeri on the west bank of the Okavango.

The Final Act records all delimitation work complete except for clearing the stretch between beacon 28 and the Okavango, planned for the next rainy season; it also provides for recurring joint inspection and maintenance.
The 1931 exchange records acceptance of the Kakeri demarcation and description as correct and recognizes the line indicated by the erected beacons.
documents.use: Primary historical boundary/survey evidence. Beacon 47 and the beacon schedule are used only for coarse contextual comparison; no current bank or river median line is reconstructed.

license.status: official League of Nations treaty-series publication hosted by the United Nations; no separate license statement captured
license.reuse_note: Retained as an official historical treaty publication for evidence and research; attribution to the League of Nations Treaty Series and United Nations Treaty Collection.

limits: The printed schedule does not state a modern geodetic datum; coordinate methods vary by beacon, and the footnote says beacon 47 latitude was not astronomically observed.
The treaty-series volume contains textual schedules but no georeferenced present-day river-bank geometry for the candidate footprints.
Historical demarcation evidence does not independently confirm current physical channel position or later state practice.

documents.title: Agreement between the Government of the Union of South Africa and the Government of the Republic of Portugal in relation to the Boundary between the Mandated Territory of South-West Africa and Angola
documents.publisher: United Kingdom Treaty Series / His Majesty's Stationery Office
relevant_content: Article 2 describes the Kunene middle line to the latitude-parallel point.
Article 3 sends that parallel east to the middle line of the Okavango (Cubango), then refers to the 1886 treaty.
Articles 4 and 6 address joint demarcation, astronomical correction, beaconing, and the river middle line where a river forms the boundary.
documents.use: Primary treaty text; legal framework, not a current georeferenced river edge.

license.status: official historical government treaty publication; no separate reuse notice captured
license.reuse_note: Retained as a whole source document for research and source review.

limits: No present-day river-bank or thalweg geometry is supplied.
The instrument refers to the 1886 Lisbon treaty for the line after the Okavango median-line intersection.

documents.title: International Boundary Study No. 120, Angola–Namibia (South-West Africa) Boundary
documents.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Geographer, Bureau of Intelligence and Research
documents.access_host: Florida State University College of Law, Research Center, Limits in the Seas archive
relevant_content: The study summarizes the boundary as the Kunene median line to Ruacana Falls, an eastward straight sector to the Okavango, then the Okavango median line.
It reports the Kakeri beacon schedule and summarizes the 1886, 1926, 1928 and 1931 instruments.
documents.use: Official secondary synthesis used as historical context and a cross-check against the primary treaty texts.

license.status: U.S. government publication; no separate document-level notice captured
license.reuse_note: Retained for research; attribution to the U.S. Department of State and the host archive.

limits: It is not itself an executed boundary instrument or a high-resolution georeferenced river line.
Its 1972 conclusions do not establish later state practice or the current river channel.

documents.title: Angola--South-West Africa boundary (Library of Congress catalog title)
documents.publisher: Library of Congress Geography and Map Division catalog record; map attributed to the Central Intelligence Agency and U.S. Department of State Office of the Geographer
documents.retrieval_status: The catalog record identifies an Angola–South-West Africa boundary map, but the linked raster was visually inspected and depicts an Angola–Zaire boundary map (latitudes around 5–12°S), not the Namibia–Angola extent. Excluded from all analysis.
documents.reason_excluded: Mismatch between cataloged title and actual raster contents; do not use as boundary evidence.
